status: canonical historical genealogy + timeline/map projection contract
purpose: Represent major religious traditions as dated, branching historical lineages. Nodes can be trunks, schisms, reforms, schools, mystical currents or institutional crystallizations. The structure is designed for timeline, spiral and map projection without pretending every tradition has one exact birthday.
epistemic_rule: Traditional/sacred origin claims, historical reconstruction, institutional dates and project visualization coordinates remain distinct. A genealogy edge describes historical relation, not theological truth, superiority, legitimacy or identity.

date_policy.exact_date: Use only for well-attested formal events such as a charter, council, declaration or organizational meeting.
date_policy.marker_year: A conventional or high-information branch marker inside a longer process; never silently treated as the whole origin.
date_policy.formation_window: Preferred for gradual crystallization, diffuse movements and retrospective denominational identities.
date_policy.deep_origin: Use broad ranges where evidence does not justify a narrow date.
date_policy.bce_encoding: Negative astronomical-style integers are used only for sorting/projection; display labels retain BCE/CE notation and do not introduce a historical year zero.

node_types.trunk: Large lineage/family with substantial historical continuity.
node_types.phase: Major historical state of a lineage before or after a transformation.
node_types.communion: Family of churches sharing communion or doctrinal/institutional identity.
node_types.denomination: Differentiated institutional tradition within a larger family.
node_types.school: Legal, philosophical or interpretive school; not automatically a separate religion.
node_types.reform_movement: Movement seeking change inside or from an inherited tradition.
node_types.schism_lineage: Lineage differentiated by a rupture or contested succession.
node_types.mystical_current: Cross-cutting current that may exist in several branches.
node_types.monastic_lineage: Transmission lineage centered on monastic institutions/practice.
node_types.sister_lineage: Related lineage with shared ancestry but not safely represented as a child.
node_types.transmission_family: Regional/cultural lineage formed through transmission of an inherited tradition plus substantial local institutional or doctrinal development.
node_types.revelatory_lineage: Lineage whose durable identity forms around a later revelation corpus or revelatory-textual movement within a broader inherited field.
node_types.tradition_field: Broad historical religious, ritual or intellectual field that precedes or exceeds one centralized institution.
node_types.institutional_phase: Historically bounded phase in which a tradition is reorganized or stabilized through institutions, state structures or formal classical systems.
node_types.intellectual_revival: Revival and reconstruction of an inherited intellectual-religious tradition after an earlier classical phase.
node_types.philosophical_school: Differentiated philosophical or interpretive school within a wider inherited tradition.
node_types.modern_intellectual_movement: Modern intellectual movement reconstructing an inherited tradition under contemporary institutional or philosophical conditions.
node_types.textual_consolidation: Phase in which texts, canons or state-sponsored compilations consolidate and frame a previously broader ritual/tradition field.
node_types.syncretic_field: Durable field formed through sustained synthesis or combinatory practice between previously distinguishable traditions.
node_types.state_reorganization: State-directed legal or institutional reorganization that substantially changes a religious field without creating it from nothing.
node_types.modern_institutional_field: Modern institutional ecology that coordinates or reorganizes an inherited tradition without reducing it to one denomination.
node_types.diffuse_religious_field: Distributed religious field with substantial local, household, temple or communal variation and no single necessary central institution.
node_types.cross_cutting_practice: Practice family that crosses ordinary institutional or lineage boundaries and may persist through several historical forms.

edge_types.differentiates_from: Identity becomes distinguishable over time without one clean break.
edge_types.splits_from: A rupture produces durable differentiated communities.
edge_types.reforms_within: Movement begins as reform of an inherited tradition.
edge_types.institutionalizes_from: A diffuse current becomes a durable institution or denomination.
edge_types.legal_school_within: Juristic school inside a broader religious family.
edge_types.mystical_current_within: Mystical/devotional current crossing ordinary institutional branches.
edge_types.communion_member: Ancient/local church participating in a later communion; not implied to have been founded when the communion divided.
edge_types.predecessor_to: Immediate historical predecessor whose identity is not simply retained.
edge_types.transmission_and_local_formation: An inherited tradition is transmitted into a new region/culture and develops a durable local lineage through both continuity and new formation.
edge_types.synthesis_with: A lineage develops through sustained synthesis with another current while retaining enough identity to remain separately traceable.
edge_types.new_movement_within_daoist_field: A new Daoist movement forms inside the broader Daoist field without implying that one earlier lineage is its sole parent.
edge_types.umbrella_consolidation: Several inherited lineages or ritual networks become coordinated under a broader institutional umbrella.
edge_types.state_sponsorship_and_classical_institut: State sponsorship, curriculum or institutions stabilize a previously broader classical/tradition field.
edge_types.revival_and_reconstruction: An inherited tradition is revived and reconstructed after an earlier phase rather than simply continuing unchanged.
edge_types.school_within: A philosophical or interpretive school differentiates within a broader tradition.
edge_types.modern_reconstruction: A modern movement reconstructs inherited materials under new intellectual, social or institutional conditions.
edge_types.textualizes_and_state_frames: Texts/canons and state framing consolidate an earlier ritual or tradition field.
edge_types.synthesis_with_buddhism: A tradition develops through durable combinatory relations with Buddhist institutions, texts or practices.
edge_types.state_separation_and_reorganization: State action separates previously combined religious fields and reorganizes their legal/institutional status.
edge_types.postwar_reorganization: A religious institutional field is reorganized after a war/political settlement under new legal conditions.
edge_types.long_continuity_and_expansion: A diffuse tradition persists over a long period while expanding or becoming more institutionally visible.
edge_types.practice_continuity: A practice continues across changing institutions and historical periods without one clean founding event.
edge_types.practice_family: A family of related practices develops across regions/communities without requiring one centralized lineage.

spiral_projection_contract.thesis: Foundation nodes unfold outward from historical time. They are not dimensions and radial distance never represents spiritual height, truth, value, age-prestige or authority.
spiral_projection_contract.radial_variable: seed_year or formation-window midpoint in a selected historical epoch transform
spiral_projection_contract.angular_variable: layout only: family and sibling separation; angle has no doctrinal ranking
spiral_projection_contract.branch_curve: child trajectory begins at its parent/ancestor branch marker and receives its own later radial trajectory
spiral_projection_contract.multi_parent_rule: Syncretic or mixed-origin nodes may connect to more than one predecessor; do not force a false single-parent tree.
spiral_projection_contract.uncertainty_render: Wide/uncertain dates render as arcs or fuzzy bands rather than exact points.
spiral_projection_contract.event_vs_foundation: Councils, destructions, migrations and succession crises may be branch events without being independent religious foundations.
spiral_projection_contract.map_link: Every node may carry an origin_place or distributed_origin for geographic projection. Present-day demographic geography remains a separate dated layer.

nodes.name: Classical Confucian / Ru textual-ritual field

seed_clock.date_or_range: Confucius traditional lifetime 551–479 BCE → Warring States classical formation

nodes.notes: Confucius is a historical teacher within a wider Ru/classical ritual world; later 'Confucianism' is a long reception history, not a religion founded in 551 BCE.

nodes.name: Han Confucian state/classical institutionalization

seed_clock.date_or_range: Han dynasty, especially from 2nd century BCE onward

nodes.notes: Confucian classics, ritual and scholar-official culture gain durable state sponsorship; this is institutionalization rather than origin.

nodes.name: Song–Ming Neo-Confucian traditions
nodes.notes: Neo-Confucian thinkers reconstruct classical ethics and ritual through new metaphysical/moral psychology partly in dialogue and competition with Buddhism and Daoism.

nodes.name: Cheng–Zhu / School of Principle

seed_clock.date_or_range: 11th–12th-century formation; Four Books exam orthodoxy by 1313

nodes.notes: Zhu Xi's synthesis and Four Books commentaries become extraordinarily influential across East Asia and later imperial examinations.

nodes.name: Lu–Wang / School of Heart-Mind
nodes.notes: Emphasizes heart-mind, innate moral knowing and the unity of knowing and acting; develops as a major alternative to Cheng-Zhu orthodoxy.

nodes.name: Modern / New Confucianism

origin.place: China / Hong Kong / Taiwan / global academy

nodes.notes: Modern thinkers reinterpret Confucian traditions in relation to modernity, democracy, science and global philosophy.

integrity: Confucianism/Ruism is simultaneously ethical, ritual, intellectual, educational and historically religious; do not force a philosophy-vs-religion binary.
State sponsorship does not make every Chinese religious practice Confucian.
Neo-Confucianism is not simply the ancient teaching of Confucius repeated unchanged.

families.name: Shinto / kami-veneration traditions

nodes.name: Ancient Japanese kami / ritual field

seed_clock.date_or_range: prehistoric/early historic Japanese ritual field → 7th century CE

nodes.notes: No founder or single foundation date; shrine/kami practices develop from diverse local, court and clan traditions.

nodes.name: Kojiki / Nihon Shoki mythic-historical textual layer
nodes.notes: Court compilations preserve and reshape mythic/genealogical traditions; they are not 'Shinto scripture' in the same sense as a canonical revealed book.

nodes.name: Shinbutsu-shūgō / kami-Buddha combinatory traditions

seed_clock.date_or_range: Nara/Heian through early modern Japan; forcibly disrupted from 1868

nodes.notes: For much of Japanese history kami and Buddhist institutions were deeply intertwined; modern images of a timelessly separate Shinto and Buddhism can obscure this history.

nodes.name: Meiji Shinto reorganization / separation
nodes.notes: Meiji policies separate kami and Buddhist institutions and reorganize shrine/state relations; later 'State Shinto' is a modern institutional-political formation.

nodes.name: Postwar Jinja Shinto

seed_clock.date_or_range: 1945 separation from state; Jinja Honcho founded 1946

nodes.notes: Most shrines associated with Jinja Honcho belong to Jinja Shinto, while distinct Sect Shinto and other organizations also exist.

integrity: Shinto has no single founder, unified creed or one scripture.
Kojiki and Nihon Shoki are major mythic/historical sources, not a simple 'Shinto Bible'.
Premodern kami worship and Buddhism were often combined; 1868 separation is a major modern rupture.

families.name: Chinese popular / communal religious field

nodes.name: Ancient ancestors, gods and divination field

origin.place: North China and wider early Chinese cultural zones

nodes.notes: Ancestor offerings, divination, gods and state/family ritual have ancient roots; no founder or denomination structure.

nodes.name: Local temple, ancestor and communal religious field

seed_clock.date_or_range: especially visible institutional expansion in Song-era commercialization/urbanization

nodes.notes: Local gods, temple associations, festivals, ancestor rites, pilgrimage, healing, divination and ritual economies overlap with Daoist, Buddhist and Confucian institutions.

nodes.name: Chinese ancestor veneration traditions
nodes.notes: Household altars, lineage halls, graveside rites and festival observances vary by period, region and community.

nodes.name: Spirit-medium, divination and geomantic practices
nodes.notes: Includes multiple regional practices; should not be treated as one church or automatically identified with formal Daoism.

integrity: Chinese popular religion is diffuse and embedded in family, village, temple, market and state life rather than a centralized church.
Practitioners may participate in Daoist, Buddhist, Confucian and local ritual worlds without exclusive membership logic.
Ancestor veneration, local-deity worship, divination and spirit-medium practice require regional and historical specificity.

cross_family_connections.note: Christianity historically emerges from the Second Temple Jewish environment while becoming a distinct tradition.
Christian communities/textual traditions formed part of the late antique environment encountered by early Islam; this is context, not a parent-child edge.
Jewish communities/traditions formed part of Arabia and the broader late-antique Near Eastern context; do not render Islam as simply a branch of Judaism.
The Bábí movement arose within a Twelver Shiʿi Persian context but became a distinct new religious movement.

future_research_queue: Christianity: deepen Baptist, Presbyterian, Congregational, Quaker, Restorationist/Latter-day Saint, African-initiated, independent and Oriental Orthodox constituent church histories.
Islam: deepen Sufi tariqas, Tayyibi/Daudi Bohra lineages, Ahmadiyya, Salafi reform currents, regional institutions and theological schools without treating all as equivalent node types.
Judaism: add Reconstructionist, Renewal, Haredi/Modern Orthodox, Sephardi/Mizrahi institutional histories and Kabbalistic schools with carefully dated formation windows.
Buddhism: add early schools, Chan/Zen, Pure Land, Tibetan schools and modern reform lineages.
Hindu traditions: expand sampradayas, Vedanta schools, bhakti movements, Tantra and regional temple lineages without inventing one universal branch tree.
Map indigenous and diasporic traditions using distributed-origin polygons/routes where a point seed would be misleading.
Attach canonical texts, councils, teachers, institutions and sacred places as separate typed nodes rather than stuffing them into tradition identity.
Add branch-by-branch geography through dated diffusion events, not current-country coloring projected backward in time.
timeline_merge_rule: Lineage seed clocks describe formation; event anchors describe notable historical states. Use branch_anchor only as a visual/historical attachment marker, never as proof the child did not exist in precursor form before that date.
